title: Audit shipper delivery models, SLA tiers, and observable retry semantics for SIEM/webhooks
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a production-grade design and implementation plan for outbound audit delivery to third-party collectors (Splunk HEC, Datadog intake, generic SIEM webhooks) that balances delivery guarantees, cost, and operational simplicity. This ticket scopes the delivery model options, observable retry/backpressure behavior, per-tenant QoS tiers, and the admin controls required to configure connectors safely (RBAC v2 + SSO/SAML gating).

Goals:
- Define clear delivery semantics per connector SLA tier (best-effort, at-least-once with dedupe, guaranteed-delivery with DLQ and retries).
- Specify idempotency and ordering strategies so downstream SIEMs can safely dedupe events when requested.
- Design observable metrics and traces for delivery latency, retry rate, DLQ volume, and tenant-level drop events.
- Ensure only authorized admin roles (via RBAC v2 and SSO group mapping) can create/modify connectors and change retention/forwarding policies.
- Provide concrete retry/backoff/backpressure model and operator runbook for connector degradation.

Constraints and non-goals:
- We will not build custom collectors inside Splunk/Datadog; integrations use standard public ingestion APIs (HEC, Datadog Logs API) or customer-provided webhook endpoints.
- This ticket covers delivery semantics and observability; connector-specific work (auth SDKs, schema adapters) will be separate sub-tasks.

Success metrics:
- <1% of audit events moved to DLQ for P1 tenants under steady-state load.
- Time-to-detect external sink outage < 1m (alert firing from connectors).
- End-to-end delivery SLA tiers documented and validated with staging tests.
acceptance_criteria: Documented delivery semantics for three QoS tiers (P0: best-effort, P1: at-least-once with dedupe token, P2: durable with DLQ and replay)
Design for idempotency tokens + sequence window to enable consumer-side dedupe
Observable dashboard and alerts (connector_up, retry_count, dlq_rate, tenant_throttle_pct) defined and prototyped
RBAC v2 policy mapping documented: which roles can create/modify connectors and which operations require SSO group membership
Operator runbook for connector failure modes and automated fallback to alternate region/variant documented
proposed_solution:
We propose an outbound shipper composed of: (1) per-tenant staging queue (in-memory + persistent journal), (2) a delivery worker pool with pluggable adapters (Splunk HEC, Datadog, generic webhook), and (3) a durable DLQ store with replay API.

Delivery tiers:
- Best-effort (P0): low-cost path, no persistent guarantees. Retries with bounded attempts (3), exponential backoff with jitter, metrics only. Intended for low-SLA customers.
- At-least-once with dedupe (P1): events carry an idempotency token (UUID) + sequence number per session. Retried indefinitely for transient errors with exponential backoff and capped concurrency to avoid thundering herd. Consumers can dedupe on token; shipper retains recent token cache (TTL) to limit DB footprint.
- Durable with DLQ (P2): persistent journal (write-ahead log) per tenant, infinite-ish retries per configured window, failed deliveries moved to tenant-scoped DLQ (configurable retention). Admins can replay DLQ via console or API.

Idempotency and ordering:
- Include fields: event_id, tenant_id, stream_id, seq_no, created_at, idempotency_key.
- For strict ordering requests, support single-shard delivery per stream with in-order processing; falls back to best-effort for high-throughput streams unless tenant purchases ordered-delivery add-on.

Backpressure and throttling:
- Per-tenant token bucket enforced before enqueueing to prevent noisy neighbor effects.
- When queue pressure crosses thresholds, emit tenant_throttle_pct and either shed low-priority events or escalate to operator-runbook depending on tier.

Observability and alerts:
- Metrics: connector_up{adapter,region}, delivery_latency_ms_p50/95/99, retry_count, dlq_rate, dedupe_rate, tenant_enqueue_depth.
- Traces: trace per delivery attempt (linkable to initial ingestion trace).
- Alerts: connector_down (5xx rate spike), dlq_rate_spike (>3x baseline), tenant_throttle_high (>10% sustained).

Admin controls and RBAC integration:
- Only roles with connector.admin scope (RBAC v2) can create/modify connectors. Connector config changes require SSO group approval for tenants with compliance flag (mapped via SAML groups).
- Audit logs for connector config changes must be written to immutable audit store and surfaced via Console.
implementation_notes: Phase 1: design doc & API contract for adapters (2 wks)
Phase 2: lightweight best-effort adapter + metrics + simple retries (3 wks)
Phase 3: idempotency cache + at-least-once flow and DLQ plumbing (4 wks)
Phase 4: RBAC v2 console controls + SSO/SAML group gating + runbook (2 wks)
Integration tests: synthetic sink that simulates 5xx spikes, slow consumers, and intermittent network partitions
